column2: the KVM_GET_DIRTY_LOG ioctl doesn't report modifications

column1: done by the host to the virtual processor areas (VPAs) and dispatch
trace logs (DTLs) registered by the guest.  This is because those
modifications are done either in real mode or in the host kernel
context
column2: and in neither case does the access go through the guest's

column1: HPT
column2: and thus no change (C) bit gets set in the guest's HPT.

column1: However
column2: the changes done by the host do need to be tracked so that

column1: the modified pages get transferred when doing live migration.  In
order to track these modifications
column2: this adds a dirty flag to the

column1: struct representing the VPA/DTL areas
column2: and arranges to set the flag

column1: when the VPA/DTL gets modified by the host.  Then
collecting the dirty log
column2: we also check the dirty flags for the

column1: VPA and DTL for each vcpu and set the relevant bit in the dirty log
if necessary.  Doing this also means we now need to keep track of
the guest physical address of the VPA/DTL areas.
So as not to lose track of modifications to a VPA/DTL area when it gets
unregistered
column2: or when a new area gets registered in its place

column1: to transfer the dirty state to the rmap chain.  This adds code to
kvmppc_unpin_guest_page() to do that if the area was dirty.  To simplify
that code
column2: we now require that all VPA
column3: DTL and SLB shadow buffer areas

column1: fit within a single host page.  Guests already comply with this
requirement because pHyp requires that these areas not cross a 4k
boundary.
